text:
maria: apiserver alerts firing in eu-west1 — lots of 503s and leader/follower lag after the GPU pool backfill. apiserver CPU at 95% on control-plane nodes, controller-manager restarting. anyone oncall?

 dave: seeing it too. etcd follower lag metric spiked around the same time as the backfill job. lots of watch events and endpoint churn.

 sre-oncall: Incident generated: apiserver_errors > 5% in eu-west1 for 3m. Runbook: https://intra.redwood/ops/runbooks/apiserver-throttling

 kevin: @maria when you have a sec can you paste recent events and autoscaler logs? curious if cluster-autoscaler backfilled excessively or if kubelets are flapping.

 maria: pasted events snippet:```
 Normal   NodeReady  kubelet, gpu-node-az1-23  Node gpu-node-az1-23 status: NotReady for 12s
 Warning  FailedMount  kubelet, gpu-node-az1-23  AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "pvc-..." : timeout
 Normal   NodeStarted kubelet, gpu-node-az1-24  Node gpu-node-az1-24 registered
 Normal   NodeReady  kubelet, gpu-node-az1-24  Node gpu-node-az1-24 status: Ready
 Warning  FailedScheduling  default-scheduler  0/20 nodes are available: 20 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu
 ```

 maria: also saw etcd metric spike: `etcd_server_proposals_committed_total` jumped 10x at backfill start.

 aurora: sounds like a "thundering registration" — hundreds of nodes register, kube-apiserver gets a flood of object updates (nodes/endpoints), watchers get overloaded. If autoscaler backfilled a few thousand GPUs at once, control-plane SLOs will break.

 alex: mitigation suggestions: 1) pause cluster-autoscaler scale-ups, 2) cordon new nodes (stop kubelets from registering), 3) reduce api-server max-burst and increase rate-limiter tokens? also consider temporary admission webhook disable for noisy controllers.

 dave: controller-manager logs show repeated timeouts watching endpoints: `watch timed out, closing` and then `panic: timed out waiting for condition` right before restart. Controller-manager restarted 3x during the spike.

 maria: I cordoned the newest GPU node group and scaled the gpu-backfill stateful job to 0. apiserver error rate dropped to ~1.8% and follower lag is decreasing.

 deploy-bot: Deploy: scaled statefulset gpu-backfill-job to 0 by @maria.

 kevin: next actions: - keep autoscaler paused until we understand quota/placement behavior - audit autoscaler config for aggressive backfill flags (e.g., balance-similar-node-groups) - open infra ticket for region quota/egress limits that may have caused zone fallback - add short-term watch-rate mitigations on apiserver (audit throttles) - schedule postmortem & cost estimate.

 aurora: cost callout: the backfill consumed ~1200 GPUs across mixed spot/on-demand — rough burn estimate ~ $120k/day while it was active. we need budget alerts on sudden capacity spikes.

 maria: filed INFRA-2345 with timeline + logs, will own postmortem. provisional follow-ups: add autoscaler circuit-breaker, add control-plane watch queue monitoring/alerting, and enforce a max-scale-per-5m policy for GPU pools.

 alex: nice triage — circle back after postmortem. for now control-plane looks stable. :thumbsup:

 dave: leaving notes in runbook about cordon + pause pattern for backfills, and adding example kubectl commands:```
 kubectl cordon <node-name>
 kubectl scale statefulset gpu-backfill-job --replicas=0 -n infra
 kubectl logs -n kube-system kube-controller-manager -f
 ```

 maria: thanks team, will update once postmortem draft is ready.
